scenes.text: Before reality becomes a fixed fact, it may exist as a field of possibilities waiting for physical contact.
scenes.query: Darkness filled with faint luminous branches, each leading toward a different distant horizon.

scenes.text: The double-slit experiment begins with a simple choice: two openings, one particle, and a screen beyond them.
scenes.query: A brass scientific apparatus assembled on a wooden table beneath a narrow shaft of morning light.

scenes.text: Send particles one at a time, and every arrival leaves one small, definite mark on that screen.
scenes.query: Individual points of light appearing slowly across a translucent glass surface.

scenes.text: But after many arrivals, those lonely marks assemble into the striped signature of waves interfering with themselves.
scenes.query: Raindrops falling separately into black water, gradually forming overlapping bands of ripples.

scenes.text: Somehow, each particle behaves as though both openings mattered, even though it was detected in only one place.
scenes.query: A polished marble approaching two doorways as translucent versions of its path divide around it.

scenes.text: It is not acting like a tiny marble that simply chooses left or right behind the curtain.
scenes.query: A mechanical marble maze freezes while its simple pathways dissolve into drifting mist.

scenes.text: It behaves more like possibility itself, spreading through every route the experiment leaves open and available.
scenes.query: Blue ink blooming through a network of branching glass channels.

scenes.text: At that stage, no road is history yet; every road still belongs to what could happen.
scenes.query: Several untouched paths crossing a field of fresh snow, none carrying footprints.

scenes.text: Then we add a detector and ask the experiment a sharper question: Which path did you take?
scenes.query: A delicate sensor arm moving into a beam chamber as indicator lights activate.

scenes.text: The interference pattern disappears, and the system gives us a route instead of overlapping possibilities.
scenes.query: Flowing bands of colored light narrowing abruptly into one clean line.

scenes.text: Reality seems to keep its options open until an interaction makes one kind of answer physically unavoidable.
scenes.query: A fan of transparent photographic plates closing until only one image remains.

scenes.text: This does not mean your thoughts command matter, or that wanting something makes the universe obey.
scenes.query: A person concentrating beside an unmoving compass while laboratory machinery operates independently behind them.

scenes.text: In physics, the observer can be a detector, a photon, or any interaction that records usable information.
scenes.query: A single photon striking a microscopic sensor and sending a pulse through copper circuitry.

scenes.text: A conscious mind is not required for the apparatus to change what the experiment can reveal.
scenes.query: An empty laboratory running automatically at midnight, monitored only by machines.

scenes.text: Certainty may be the product that appears only after possibility meets a boundary, a measurement, or a collision.
scenes.query: Molten metal flowing into a rigid geometric mold and cooling into one solid form.

scenes.text: What we call an event may be one path becoming visible while the alternatives stop interfering with it.
scenes.query: Many transparent rivers overlap before condensing into one river cutting through a canyon.

scenes.text: Beneath every fact, nature may have carried more futures than the single one that finally became our past.
scenes.query: Branching timelines suspended inside amber, with one branch hardening into a bright golden thread.
